info.description: Host driving contract for the Apollia OS sovereign agent runtime. Stable under /api/v1; breaking changes ship under /api/v2.

post.summary: Handler for `POST /api/v1/a2a/invoke`.

that takes a message (`agent:<id>`) or a workflow
(`workflow:<package>/<name>`), and answers once it has ended.
Returns 503 if the invoker is not initialized.
Returns 404 if the skill is not found, 503 if the agent is not active,
400 if the input does not fit what the target takes.

post.summary: Handler for `POST /api/v1/agents`.
post.description:
Loads the Python agent module via [`AgentLoader`], validates
AIP duck typing, registers the agent with its real manifest, transitions
to Active (or Degraded if optional tools are missing), and creates an
[`ExecutionCoordinator`] registered with the [`TaskRouter`].

Tool resolution is delegated to [`apollia_tools::resolve`] which handles
the `a2a:` prefix correctly (A2A dependencies live in the ToolProxy
allowed_tools list, not in the ToolRegistry, and must not trigger
DEGRADED). A missing `tools_required` entry returns 400 Bad Request.

Returns 201 Created with the agent_id and state.
Returns 400 Bad Request if the Python module is invalid.

200.description: Installed agents with their runtime state, then agents started without being installed

500.description: agents.db or the registry cannot be read

post.summary: Handler for `POST /api/v1/agents/installed`.
post.description: Emits `RuntimeEvent::AgentInstalled` once the agent is recorded.

put.summary: Handler for `PUT /api/v1/agents/installed/{name}`.
put.description:
Validates the new module, replaces the installed one, records the new
version, and cycles the runtime instance when there is one. The cycle is the
point of the route: the interpreter holds the module it imported at start
time, so without the stop and the start the window would report a new
version while the old one keeps answering. Emits
`RuntimeEvent::AgentInstalled` once the runtime has settled.

200.description: Agent updated, with what happened to its running instance

404.description: No installed agent of that name

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/agents/installed/{name}/uninstall`: uninstall an agent
installed on its own.
post.description:
Removes the agent, its overrides, its model, its triggers, its
environment and its files. Its memory and history are erased only when
the body asks. Apollia cannot be uninstalled; an agent of an installed
package goes with its package.

409.description: The agent belongs to an installed package

get.description:
Returns the detail of a single agent including its manifest.
Accepts both a UUID and a human-readable agent name (e.g. `apollia-reviewer`).

delete.summary: Handler for `DELETE /api/v1/agents/{id}`.
delete.description:
Performs a full graceful shutdown of the agent:
1. Transitions to `Stopping` (emits `AgentStopping` event for observers).
2. Unregisters the `ExecutionCoordinator` from the `TaskRouter` so no new
   tasks can be submitted to this agent.
3. Transitions to `Stopped` (emits `AgentStopped` event).

This mirrors the sequence performed by [`ShutdownController::stop_agents`]
during full system shutdown. The `Stopping` intermediate state is preserved
so that event-bus subscribers (dashboard, SSE streams) observe the correct
lifecycle.

Accepts both a UUID and a human-readable agent name (e.g. `apollia-reviewer`).
Returns 409 Conflict if the agent is already stopped or stopping.
Returns 404 if the agent does not exist.

409.description: Agent already stopped or stopping

Returns `503` when the mailbox is not available.

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/audit/anchor`, the exportable head anchor of the global chain.
get.description:
Storing this off-machine is the only defense against truncation of the
global tail once the signing key can be compromised. Returns 404 when the
journal has no entries yet, 503 when the journal is not configured.

get.summary:
`GET /api/v1/audit/journal?limit=N&offset=M`, a page of the chained journal
across every run, each entry with its summary.
get.description:
This is the only read of the journal that does not need a run id up front:
`GET /api/v1/audit/journal/{run_id}` answers a run the caller already knows,
and `GET /api/v1/audit` answers the separate tool-invocation trail. The
filters are applied before paging, so `limit` and `offset` count matching
entries. 400 on a filter value that cannot be read, 503 when the journal is
not configured.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default 20, capped at 500)

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of matching entries to skip, newest first (default 0). Page through the journal by advancing it.

parameters.name: agents
parameters.description: Comma-separated agent names. When set, only the entries that name one of those agents, and the runs of their tasks, are paged.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Start of the period, included: a day `YYYY-MM-DD` read in UTC, or an RFC 3339 instant.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: End of the period, excluded: a day `YYYY-MM-DD` read in UTC, or an RFC 3339 instant.

200.description: A page of hash-chained journal entries, each with its summary

400.description: A filter value that cannot be read

503.description: Audit journal not configured, or `agents` given with no task repository to resolve them

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/audit/journal/:run_id`, the full journal for a run.
get.description:
Unlike `GET /api/v1/audit` (the tool-only audit trail), this returns the
hash-chained journal entries including `llm_completion` (the model's
prompts/responses). 404 when the run has no entries, 503 when the journal is
not configured.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: Run id whose journal entries are returned

200.description: Full hash-chained journal for the run

get.description:
The page gives each entry a summary without content. This gives the entry
whole and, for a tool call, the full arguments and the full output of that
call, joined by the run and the call identifier from the entries the run
captured for replay. 404 when the run has no such entry, 503 when the
journal is not configured.

parameters.name: seq
parameters.description: Sequence number of the entry within its run

200.description: The entry, its summary, and the arguments and output of its tool call when it is about one

404.description: The run has no such entry

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/audit/replay/:run_id`, replay a captured run and report
determinism.
post.description:
Resolves the run id (full or unambiguous prefix), runs the
[`ReplayHarness`], and returns a JSON body with a `status` discriminant:
`identical`, `diverged`, or `error`. Status codes: 200 for identical and
diverged (the determinism verdict is in the body), 404 for an unknown run,
400 for an ambiguous prefix, 422 for an incomplete trace, 503 when the
journal is not configured.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: Run id (full or unambiguous prefix) to replay

422.description: Incomplete trace

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/audit/stats`, aggregate counts for the audit trail.
`GET /api/v1/audit/verify`, verify the whole journal across all runs.
get.description:
Unlike the per-run route, this walks the global chain (detecting interior
deletion and whole-run deletion) and compares the terminal head to the
persisted anchor (detecting global-tail truncation). An empty journal is a
valid 200 `ok:true`, not a 404. Returns 503 when the journal is not
configured and 500 on an internal error.

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/audit/verify/:run_id`, verify a run's hash chain and signatures.
get.description:
Returns 200 with the [`VerifyChainReport`] (whether or not the chain is
intact), 404 when the run has no entries, 503 when the journal is not
configured, and 500 on an internal error.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: Run id whose hash chain is verified

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many batches, 50 when absent.

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/batches`: launch an agent on every item of a source.
post.description:
The items are read and recorded before the answer; they run in the
background, at most `concurrency` at once (1 by default, 16 at most).
Once more than `maxFailures` items have failed (10 by default), the
batch is interrupted: no further item starts.

`GET /api/v1/batches/accesses`: the sensitive accesses of an agent, those
a launch may grant for the duration of a batch.
get.description:

`grantable` (executing code, or an access nobody classified) is listed
too: an item that reaches for it waits for a decision.

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/batches/{id}/export`: the result of a batch as a file.

workbook of one sheet, `csv` is UTF-8 with one header row, `json` is one
document with the batch and an object per item. The file is offered as
`batch-<id>.<format>`. A batch still running exports the items as they
stand.

post.summary: Handler for `POST /api/v1/llm/chat`.
post.description:
Builds a single-turn `CompletionRequest` from the prompt and dispatches it
via `LlmRouter::complete_with_observability`. Observability events
(`LlmCallCompleted`) are emitted on the `EventBus` automatically.

Returns `503 Service Unavailable` if no router is configured or the call fails.

409.description: A local model the load guardrail refused; confirm the load to go ahead

503.description: No router configured or backend call failed

post.summary: Handler for `POST /api/v1/llm/complete`.
post.description:
Accepts a multi-turn conversation history and dispatches it through
`LlmRouter::complete_with_observability`. Each `MessageDto` is mapped
to a `ChatMessage` based on its `role` field:

- `"system"`    → `ChatMessage::system`
- `"user"`      → `ChatMessage::user`
- `"assistant"` → `ChatMessage::assistant`
- `"tool"`      → `ChatMessage::tool_result` (empty call id)

Returns `400 Bad Request` when an unknown role is encountered.
Returns `503 Service Unavailable` when no router is configured or the call fails.

409.description: A local model the load guardrail refused; confirm the load to go ahead

503.description: No router configured or backend call failed

get.description:

invocation_id.description:
A name the client chooses for this invocation, so it can cancel it.

finished, so the task id it returns arrives too late to cancel
anything. A name supplied here is bound to the task as soon as the task
is submitted, and `DELETE /api/v1/tasks/{id}` accepts it in place of the
task id until this call returns. The invocation then answers `409` with
a cancellation error instead of running to its timeout.

runs normally and the journal says so (`a2a.invocation_id.taken`).

bearerAuth.description: Token read from `<data_dir>/api-token`, generated on first start and sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Enforced on the TCP listener by `TokenAuthLayer`, on every route except two: `GET /api/v1/health`, which reveals the product marker and the version only, and `POST /webhooks/{id}`, which authenticates its caller with an HMAC-SHA256 signature instead. Requests arriving on the Unix socket bypass the check: the socket file is mode 0600, so its permissions carry the same rule. Setting `[api] require_token = false` in `apollia.toml` removes the layer from the TCP listener altogether.
